defect.summary: Eng reads whether OUTCOME depends on EVENT CLASS and compares the result to a declared structureThreshold, gated only by minimumSampleSize — A COUNT OF ROWS. A chain can satisfy that count while carrying almost no class variety: 600 rows of which 598 are one class and two are singletons passes the floor and is read as a structure finding. The three ARITY gates below it (fewer than 2 distinct classes, no class recurring, a non-positive AMI denominator) catch only the degenerate end; between 'degenerate' and 'enough to read' there is no rule at all, and minimumSampleSize has been standing in for one. FIX: a DECLARED coverage floor. At least k distinct observed classes must each carry at least k events, k injected, no default. Below it Eng returns CANNOT_ASSESS/INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE and does not read. ⛔ THE RULE IS THE LOOSER OF THE TWO READINGS AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: 'at least k classes each with at least k events', NOT 'every observed class has at least k events'. The stricter reading lets ONE rare class block the read forever, which recreates the unsatisfiability defect found the same day on the declared-class axis — five declared lineClasses, one occupied subject, so 'every declared class ≥ k' can never be met and would hold the deployment permanently on an artefact of the declaration's shape.

arbiter.word: I, the arbiter, grant T11: Eng must refuse to read a chain that does not carry at least k distinct observed event classes each with at least k events, k declared and no default; granted because a row count is not a variety rule, and a reader that answers 'does outcome depend on class' over a table with almost no class variety is reporting an arithmetic result as a finding.

conditions: PRE-REGISTRATION, WRITTEN BEFORE ANY CODE. The rule is: count the observed classes (moduleId, eventType) that carry >= k events; if that count is < k, return CANNOT_ASSESS with INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE and do not read. k is INJECTED as readers.eng.minimumClassCoverage with NO DEFAULT — absent, Eng returns CANNOT_ASSESS/MISSING_CONFIGURATION exactly as it already does for structureThreshold and minimumSampleSize. A default k would be a calibration constant, and calibration is not this build's to make.

⛔ PLACEMENT IS PART OF THE TICKET, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL, AND IT WAS MEASURED. The check goes AFTER all three arity gates (distinctClasses < 2, !hasRepeatedClass, ami === null) and BEFORE the A5 ceiling. Placed before them instead, a single-class record reports 'insufficient coverage' rather than INELIGIBLE_SCOPE, and the coarser refusal MASKS the more specific and more truthful one. MEASURED 2026-09-30 by running the probe in both positions: placed early it moved 5 assertions across 3 suites ([INELIGIBLE_SCOPE] a single event class, no class recurs, and two D-24 diagnostics rows); placed correctly it moves NONE.

THE COUNT IS TAKEN LOCALLY, NOT FROM engDiagnostics. A4 diagnostics are computed and, in the file's own words, 'NEVER consulted below' — every branch from that point reads `structure`, `threshold` and `ceilingMargin` only. `perClass` already carries exactly these counts, which is precisely why reading it here would be the easy wrong move: it would make a verdict depend on the diagnostic channel and quietly end that invariant.

⛔ WHAT A FAIL LOOKS LIKE, pre-registered, with the arbiter's own first line: (a) THE RULE HOLDS A CHAIN WHOSE OBSERVED CLASSES ARE ALL >= 3 — a false hold is the failure that matters, because it is the one that looks like diligence; (b) k absent is treated as a default rather than MISSING_CONFIGURATION; (c) the refusal is reported as ALARM or as a structure reading rather than CANNOT_ASSESS; (d) a single-class record stops reporting INELIGIBLE_SCOPE, i.e. the placement condition was not honoured; (e) STRUCK 2026-10-01 — SEE THE TWO AMENDMENT CONDITIONS AT THE END OF THIS LIST; (f) substrate-snapshot.test.ts moves; (g) the door reports drift on any file not in `opens`.
